text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and finding the pagination code.
The bug is visible at line 31: `end` is computed as `start + page_size - 1`, and then it's used as a slice bound (likely exclusive), dropping one item per page. Let me read the file to confirm.

Confirmed: `items[start:end]` with `end = start + page_size - 1` is exclusive on the right, so each page drops the element at index `start + page_size - 1`. That's the element at every 5th position (indices 4, 9, ...), matching the "regular interval" in the report. The last page with 11 items gives `items[10:10]` = empty, so item 11 is also lost. The fix is to make `end` the full page span.
All 29 tests pass. Let me finish.

args.summary: Fixed an off-by-one in `library/pagination.py::paginate`. The slice end was computed as `start + page_size - 1`, but Python slice ends are exclusive, so every page silently dropped the item at its last position (indices 4, 9, 14, ... for page size 5), and the final partial page lost its last item too. That's why the same items went missing at a regular interval. Changed the end to `start + page_size`. The full test suite passes (29 tests). With 11 items and page size 5, pages now return [1..5], [6..10], [11], covering all 11 SKUs.
